newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Nov 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Nov 21.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on Thursday:
WASHINGTON - House Speaker Newt Gingrich was unanimously reelected the House Republicans' leader and promised a conciliatory approach in dealing with the Clinton administration.
WASHINGTON - Three people were killed on the Bay Bridge in Maryland, forcing officials to close down the west-bound span of the four-mile bridge for three hours.

WASHINGTON - A three-year-old Virginia girl was critically injured after her father waged a rush-hour traffic duel with another driver on Interstate 95 that ended in a three-car crash in Prince William County.

WASHINGTON - Federal and auto industry officials suspected as long ago as 1969 that air bags could kill some children and small adults, but the government did not disclose the information as it campaigned for widespread acceptance of the devices, said documents spanning 20 years of debate over air bags.
WASHINGTON - The largest international study ever undertaken on how American students perform in math and science shows that their work lags behind many other nations.

WASHINGTON - The sexual abuse of female trainees by drill instructors at the Aberdeen Proving Ground is less an anomaly than part of a long-standing problem with trainers that the Army, until now, has tried to keep to itself.
WASHINGTON - Maryland Gov. Parris Glendening is developing a new program that would pay college tuition for many high school students who maintain B-average grades.
